method.value: Weight each residual image by its MAD, apply clean masks, sum in Jy/beam; produce 6 and 3 arcsec stacks of nine targets

evidence.quote: We stacked the source subtracted ALMA images by first measuring the median absolute deviation (MAD) of each residual image and applying weighting to each residual image based on the MAD.
All the residuals were then stacked by summation in units of Jy/beam.
masked regions were not included in the stack.

analysis_steps.goal: Convert stacked flux to Compton y

method.value: Interpret stacked continuum decrement as thermal SZE and convert to Compton parameter using the Sazonov & Sunyaev formulation

evidence.quote: We interpret the stacked continuum flux observations as SZE signal by converting to Compton parameter
For stacked QSO environments we use a pure thermal SZE model to determine the Compton parameters.
Our stacking analysis will not be sensitive to the non-spherically symmetric kSZE.

claims.hypothesis: Do the stacked quasars sit in massive virialized halos that would produce a thermal SZE decrement?
claims.experiment: Compare the stacked y radial profile with ALMA-simulated gNFW halo models of four masses
claims.result: Higher mass models become statistically less consistent; the 1e13 Msun model has p = 0.09
claims.finding: Halo mass of the stack <1e13 Msun (90% confidence), consistent with ~3e12 Msun clustering estimates

evidence.quote: Looking at Table 2 we can see that as we go to higher halo mass models, it becomes statistically less likely that they are consistent with our observations.

claims.hypothesis: Do thermal AGN wind bubbles contribute a detectable SZE around the stacked quasars?
claims.experiment: Compare the 3 arcsec stack radial profile with simulated spherical wind models of several powers and ages
claims.result: Higher power models are less consistent; at 1e12 Lsun and T = 1e8 yr p = 0.01
claims.finding: Wind power <1e12 Lsun, about <1% of the quasar bolometric luminosity

evidence.quote: Looking at Tables 3 and 4 we see that in both outflow age cases, as we go to higher power models, it becomes statistically less likely that they are consistent with our observations.

claims.hypothesis: Is there a significant SZE signal in the stacked ALMA continuum?
claims.experiment: Stack MAD-weighted residual images of nine QSOs and convert to Compton y
claims.result: Peak y of (1.7 +/- 1.1)e-6; best-fitting models chi-square similar to zero signal
claims.finding: No significant detection; further model fitting is not merited by these data

evidence.quote: Further fitting of halo and feedback models is therefore not merited by the data available in this survey.

referee_caveats_inferred: Manual masking of sources and removal of the QSO via clean may bias residual y at small radii and the central bins are dropped
Radial bins are wider than the beam so neighboring bins are partly correlated, yet chi-square treats them as independent
The reported peak y (1.7 +/- 1.1)e-6 is about 1.5 sigma, so the 'measurement' is not a detection
Quoted 90% confidence from a p-value of 0.09 is a loose threshold
Model comparison depends on assumed concentration of 1 and fixed outflow ages
Dust emission from the QSO hosts could contaminate the Band 4 decrement and is not modeled

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: About 10 EBs of 1-2 hours of Band 4 12m data; roughly 100-300 GB raw, 20-50 GB calibrated
reproducibility.score_reason: ALMA project code and CASA/pipeline versions are given and key imaging settings (robust 0.5, pixel size, tapers) are stated, but masks, thresholds, stacking details, y conversion and simulation setup are missing.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Data are public via project 2019.1.01251.S, but the manual masking, simulator setup and chi-square binning are not specified well enough to recover the numeric results reliably.
